memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of migraine and osteoporosis.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports occasional throbbing frontal headaches, relieved by sumatriptan, and no new bone pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 58 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 24.2 (overweight). Neurologic exam normal; no focal deficits. Spine tender minimally over lumbar region.
IMPRESSION: Migraine controlled on prophylactic propranolol; osteoporosis stable on alendronate, calcium and vitamin D. Advised weight management and daily walk.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, topiramate 25 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg SOS; alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium 500 mg BD with vitamin D3. Return if headache worsens, visual aura, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: CT head (non‑contrast): No acute hemorrhage, infarct or mass lesion. Ventricles and sulci age‑appropriate. No evidence of chronic ischemic changes.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Allergy: Penicillin – rash and pruritus within 30 minutes of ingestion. Avoid beta‑lactam antibiotics.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Increase in migraine frequency.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports 4‑5 migraine days per month, needing sumatriptan twice weekly; mild neck stiffness.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/84 mmHg, weight 59 kg, BMI 24.5 (overweight). Neurologic exam normal; no meningismus.
IMPRESSION: Migraine prophylaxis may need uptitration. Osteoporosis unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase topiramate to 50 mg HS; continue propranolol, sumatriptan, naproxen, osteoporosis meds. Advise low‑salt diet, regular aerobic activity. Return if headache becomes daily, neurological deficit, vision changes, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Autumn review; influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stable migraine (2‑3 days/month) with sumatriptan use; no new bone pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/80 mmHg, weight 59 kg, BMI 24.5 (overweight). Lung clear, heart regular S1S2.
IMPRESSION: Migraine controlled on current regimen. Osteoporosis stable; vitamin D sufficient. Influenza vaccine indicated due to age >60.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, topiramate 50 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg SOS; alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium 500 mg BD with vitamin D3. Administered inactivated influenza vaccine (0.5 mL IM) today. Return if headache worsens, neurological signs, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been having more throbbing headaches lately, especially after long drives. Sumatriptan helps but I need it almost every other day. Worried about medicine overuse.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Review of increased migraine frequency and medication overuse concern.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports migraine on 8‑10 days/month, using sumatriptan 4‑5 times weekly; mild nausea after doses.
EXAMINATION: BP 142/86 mmHg, weight 60 kg, BMI 25.0 (obese). Neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Probable medication‑overuse headache contributing to migraine burden. Osteoporosis unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop sumatriptan SOS; start naproxen 500 mg BD for acute migraine with gastroprotection if needed; keep propranolol 40 mg OD, topiramate 50 mg HS. Continue osteoporosis meds. Counsel on limiting acute meds to <10 days/month, hydration, regular sleep. Return if headache becomes daily, neurological deficit, vision loss, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.

Fasting blood sugar: 90 mg/dL (normal).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Six‑month follow‑up after medication‑overuse intervention.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports migraine days reduced to 4‑5 per month, sumatriptan use nil; occasional mild headache relieved by naproxen.
EXAMINATION: BP 139/82 mmHg, weight 59.5 kg, BMI 24.8 (overweight).
IMPRESSION: Migraine improved after limiting acute medication; osteoporosis stable on alendronate, calcium, vitamin D.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, topiramate 50 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg BD PRN; alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium 500 mg BD with vitamin D3. Discuss fall prevention, weight‑bearing exercise. Return if headache worsens, neurological signs, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.
